clue.text: Diversions resulting from pontoon bridge splitting

definitions.text: Diversions resulting from pontoon bridge splitting

parts.words: Diversions resulting from pontoon bridge splitting
parts.note: split the phrase 'pontoon bridge' into its two words and each names a pastime played with a pack

explanation.surface: Traffic is diverted because a floating military crossing has broken apart.
explanation.walkthrough: A pontoon bridge is a floating crossing of boats, but pontoon (blackjack) and bridge are each games with a pack, so splitting the phrase yields two such diversions.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontoon and bridge are both pastimes played with a pack of fifty-two, so they are diversions of that kind.

clue.text: Squeeze some energy out of host on ship

indicators.note: taking something out of a word removes it, here a single E

parts.note: a compere is the host of a show
E is the physics symbol for energy
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Drain some vigour from a presenter aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' takes away just one of the host's two Es; the answer decides which, as the ship's letters follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To compress is to squeeze something into a smaller space.

clue.text: One responsible for capital ancient region raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means written upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: Sumer was an ancient region of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Someone built a great city in a land of old that was lifted up.
explanation.walkthrough: Remus and his twin Romulus were the legendary founders of Rome, the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend the twins Romulus and Remus founded Rome, so he shares credit for that capital.

clue.text: Sporting achievement in which opponents never regain the lead

definitions.text: Sporting achievement in which opponents never regain the lead

parts.words: Sporting achievement in which opponents never regain the lead
parts.note: in bridge, a side that takes every trick never lets the opposition lead again, a feat also named in tennis and rugby

explanation.surface: A team wins so thoroughly the other side never goes ahead again.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the player who wins a trick leads to the next, so winning all thirteen tricks means the opponents never get the lead back.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning all thirteen tricks at bridge, or all four majors in tennis, is the supreme feat of that name.

clue.text: Broken stones gardener put under cover

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece put under another is written below it

parts.note: a mac (mackintosh) is a raincoat, a cover
Adam was the first gardener, in Eden

explanation.surface: A gardener sets some crushed rocks beneath a sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: Macadam is a road surface of broken stones laid in layers.

clue.text: In course taken initially, study very little

parts.note: soup is typically the first course of a meal
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: In the first course of a meal, there is scarcely any learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but it describes soup as the course eaten first.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupcon is a tiny amount, a trace, from the French for suspicion.

clue.text: One water-bird on river is mature

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece set on another is written after it

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A swan on the river is fully grown.
explanation.definitionFit: To mature and to ripen are synonyms for developing fully, as fruit does.

clue.text: The thinking man's sculptor

parts.note: plays on 'the thinking man's X' as a highbrow choice, while pointing at the artist of the famous seated figure called The Thinker

explanation.surface: This sculptor is the intellectual's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The French sculptor made The Thinker, a statue of a man deep in thought.

clue.text: Having nothing, under pressure, book slogger's put in?

definitions.text: Having nothing, under pressure, book slogger's put in?

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece under another is written below it

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: one piece put in another sits inside it

parts.note: a toiler is one who slogs; the 's is the link 'has'

explanation.surface: A hack under financial pressure has churned out a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' sets B inside TOILER to make TBOILER after PO. The whole clue also describes the hack writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a book dashed off for money, written by a hard-up hack.

clue.text: Kind mother, so-called

definitions.meaning: kind as a noun means sort or character

explanation.definitionFit: Nature means essential character or sort, and the natural world is called Mother Nature.

clue.text: Child's mother holding black snake

indicators.note: one word holding another wraps around it, so the letters for black sit inside

parts.note: MAMA is what a child calls its mother
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A youngster's mum is clutching a dark serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: A mamba is a venomous African snake, the black mamba being the best known.

clue.text: Firm date put out for hostile takeover

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: letters put out are thrown out of order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A company announces the date set for an aggressive bid to acquire a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The business language misleads: 'hostile takeover' is not a company bid but a seizure of government, and 'out' signals that the date and put letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a sudden seizure of state power, a takeover of government by force.

clue.text: Lived somewhere like Liverpool?

parts.note: the first word gives the meaning 'dwelt', while the rest hints at a football club known as the Reds, a red side

explanation.surface: Someone once made their home in a city such as Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool FC are nicknamed 'the Reds', so Liverpool is a red side; the letters of RED SIDE also make the answer, a playful nod rather than strict wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to live in a place, so having dwelt somewhere is the past tense of that verb.

clue.text: Openness of university with positive attitude? Right

parts.note: a can-do attitude is a positive, willing one

explanation.surface: A university boasts frankness about its upbeat outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Candour is frankness, openness in speech and dealing.

clue.text: Flexible in thought, in way that's enhancing

parts.note: supple means flexible, bending easily
mentally means in the mind, in thought

explanation.surface: Being nimble-minded is a way of improving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supplementary adds to or enhances, so acting in that manner is adding extra.

clue.text: Put together a lot of data for pub facility, perhaps

parts.note: to pool is to put resources together
a table is a set of data in rows and columns

explanation.surface: Gather lots of figures to plan a bar's amenities.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool table is found in many pubs, an example of the amenities they offer.

clue.text: Try again to meet this person's request

definitions.text: Try again to meet this person's request

parts.words: Try again to meet this person's request
parts.note: 'try' is meant in its legal sense: hearing a case again in a higher court is what this litigant asks for

explanation.surface: Have another go to satisfy someone's demand.
explanation.definitionFit: An appellant is one who appeals to a higher court for a case to be heard again.

clue.text: Set of characters female encountered in would-be dominant church

indicators.note: a piece encountered in another is met inside it

parts.note: a Type A personality is ambitious and competitive, wanting to dominate
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A woman is met in a church eager to dominate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would-be dominant' stands for the Type A personality, ambitious and competitive; 'encountered in' places the female letter inside it and the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface is a designed set of printed letters, a font.

clue.text: Bad run symptomatic of what makes red cells proliferate?

indicators.note: a bad version of the letters is a corrupted one, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor run of results is typical of an illness that multiplies red blood cells.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical picture misleads: 'red cells' are communist cells, and the organisation that spreads them is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Communists were called reds and organised in cells, so the political organisation multiplies them.

clue.text: State of knower, confused about unknown

indicators.note: one piece about another goes around it
confused letters are mixed up and reordered

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone wise is muddled about something unfamiliar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' makes NEWORK from KNOWER; 'about' puts it around Y.
explanation.definitionFit: New York is one of the fifty US states.

clue.text: Act like supporters in part of ground not far away

parts.note: a stand is a section of a sports ground for spectators
by means near, close at hand

explanation.surface: Fans behave as fans do in a section of the stadium nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand by someone is to support them loyally.

clue.text: Sun exposed this high-flier's mistake

parts.note: reads like a tabloid revealing a tycoon's error, but describes the myth of the boy whose wax wings melted when he flew too near the sun

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper revealed a successful executive's blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, which makes the clue look like a news story.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this son of Daedalus flew too close to the sun, which melted his wings.

clue.text: Person used to be seen in musical, with a piano backing

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: Someone appears in a stage show accompanied by a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's-paw is someone exploited as a tool by another, from the fable of the monkey and the cat.

clue.text: Piece of wood, a selection of which is put in box

definitions.meaning: a flat board set into a door or wall

definitions.text: a selection of which is put in box
definitions.meaning: a list of potential jurors, from which the jury in the jury box is chosen

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a flat board and a list of people from which a jury is picked.

clue.text: Line in a great novel, unbound

indicators.note: one piece put in another sits inside it
novel means new, so these words are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sentence appears in a celebrated work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' makes ATARGE from A GREAT; 'in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal at large is free and not confined, so unbound in the sense of loose.

clue.text: Page three, for example, churchman finally eliminated

indicators.note: the churchman has his final letter eliminated, cut from the end

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A tabloid's topless page sees a clergyman dismissed in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Page three, notorious in the Sun tabloid, is here just an odd-numbered page; 'finally eliminated' drops the last R.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand page of an open book, always odd-numbered like page three.

clue.text: Hold up popular poet as one favouring wealth redistribution

parts.note: to hold up is to rob at gunpoint
in means popular, fashionable
Thomas Hood was a nineteenth-century English poet

explanation.surface: A well-loved poet is waylaid in a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: The outlaw of legend stole from the rich to give to the poor, redistributing wealth.

clue.text: Seas are hidden by 'aze, reportedly, in this port

indicators.note: one piece hidden by another is enclosed within it
reportedly means as heard spoken, so the dropped-aitch word is taken by its sound

parts.note: haze with its H dropped sounds like 'A's', two letter As
said quickly, these words sound like the letters C, C and R

explanation.surface: The oceans are obscured by mist, as a Cockney might say, at this harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces work by sound: 'Seas are' is heard as C's R, and the Cockney 'aze as A's; 'hidden by' puts CCR between the two As.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra, the capital of Ghana, is a port on the Gulf of Guinea.

clue.text: Indicate period charm

definitions.meaning: letters ... a word indicate it, as in 'C-A-T ... cat'

explanation.surface: Show the hour of a magic charm.
explanation.definitionFit: The word has three senses: to signify, a stretch of time, and an incantation.

clue.text: Writer's depression getting character on to screen

definitions.text: Writer's depression getting character on to screen

parts.words: Writer's depression getting character on to screen
parts.note: not a writer's gloom but the pressing down of a key by a typist, which puts a letter on the display

explanation.surface: A novelist's block lifts as they get a hero filmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Each press of a keyboard key enters a character, so it is a typist's pressing down.
